/$defs/runtimeValue.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/0.explanation: A literal scalar argument; $calc arithmetic accepts only finite numbers, so strings, booleans and null fail when evaluated.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1.explanation: An array argument, typically a literal or partly computed vector such as [0, 0, {"$axis": "z"}], or six-number bounds.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1/items.explanation: One $calc argument: a literal number, string, boolean or null, an array of such values (for example a vector), or a nested runtime expression.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/2.explanation: A runtime expression: a JSON object that replaces a whole option or camera value and is evaluated for each state after upstream nodes are updated. In Blender documents it can read an axis value ($axis), the time ($time) or an updated node's observation ($observe), and combine them with $calc arithmetic or registered $call functions. The result must still satisfy the destination field. Constructor settings (reader file and scale, curveFromCSV file) cannot use it, and field sampling ($sample) is not available in Blender.

fields.explanation: Renders a saved Schemaxis Blender scene (a .blend published by a schemaxis.blender/1 run) from new cameras without rebuilding its geometry. It opens a retained copy of the file, replaces lighting and render settings with this document's, frames each camera on the saved visible meshes and writes one PNG per camera; verification checks that geometry and materials were unchanged by rendering.
pitfalls: Only scenes saved by Schemaxis work: the file must carry its node metadata, have no linked libraries and pack all images.

/properties/version.explanation: Identifies the document format and chooses its adaptor. Keep the version matching the selected schema.

/properties/sceneFile.explanation: The saved .blend to render, normally {"$artifact": producer, "index": n} pointing at the scene artifact of a prepareOnly Blender operation. A literal path is resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; the file is copied into the run directory and its SHA-256 is checked again at verification.
/properties/sceneFile.label: Saved scene
pitfalls: The artifact index counts images and meshes before the .blend of each state; with prepareOnly and no meshes, state 0's .blend is index 0.

/properties/cameras.explanation: Literal camera views (1 to 1000), each rendered to {index}.png in list order. Runtime expressions are not available here because the saved scene is not re-evaluated.
/properties/cameras.label: Cameras

/properties/cameras/items.explanation: One camera view. Each camera produces one PNG per render job, framed on the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene unless bounds, focalPoint, scale or distance are given. Omitted settings mean: view from +x, Z up, orthographic, automatic fit with 10% padding.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Which side of the subject the camera looks from: Blender places the camera at focalPoint + unit(direction) x distance and points it back at the focal point. "x+" or [1, 0, 0] views from +x; [1, -2, 1] gives a raised front-right view. Give an axis token, a vector, or an azimuth/elevation object.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: View direction
pitfalls: It must not be parallel to up; for views straight down use direction "z+" with up "y+".

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: A camera direction of "z+" or "z-" is parallel to the default up [0, 0, 1] and fails with INVALID_CAMERA; set up to "y+" for top or bottom views.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

Object spelling: give exactly one of axis (a token), vector, or azimuth and elevation, optionally with up as the reference axis for the angles. Choose it when a direction is easier to state as compass angles, e.g. {"azimuth": 30, "elevation": 20} for the direction 30 degrees anticlockwise from +x (seen from above) and 20 degrees above the horizontal plane. The resolved unit vector gives the side of the subject the camera is placed on: Blender puts the camera at focalPoint + direction x distance, looking back at the focal point.
pitfalls: Combining axis, vector and angles in one object fails with OVER_SPECIFIED_DIRECTION.
An omitted azimuth or elevation is taken as 0.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis
Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up
Direction as a world-axis vector [x, y, z] inside the object form; normalised, so only its direction matters. Do not combine it with axis, azimuth or elevation.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: Vector

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: One world-axis component of the object's vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

Reference axis for azimuth and elevation in this object: azimuth turns anticlockwise about it (seen from its positive side) starting from +x, or from +y when the reference is along x, and elevation tilts towards it. It is not the camera's screen-up setting.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.label: Angle reference axis

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dir.explanation: Reference axis as a token such as "z+" or "y+"; choose it when angles should be measured about a world axis.
Reference axis as a vector [x, y, z], normalised; choose it when angles should be measured about a tilted axis, such as a vehicle's own vertical.
One world-axis component of the reference axis vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up.explanation: Which world direction appears upwards in the image. Only its part perpendicular to the view direction is used, so [0, 0, 1] keeps world Z vertical for any side view.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up.label: Screen up
pitfalls: An up parallel to direction fails with INVALID_CAMERA.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Axis-token spelling: names a world axis and sign, e.g. "x+", "y-" or "z+" (also "x", "+x", "xp", "xm", "-x"; case-insensitive). Choose it for directions along world axes, such as standard front, side or top views; here the token gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.

Vector spelling [x, y, z] in world axes; only its direction matters, Schemaxis normalises it. Choose it for oblique views or directions computed elsewhere; here it gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.
pitfalls: [0, 0, 0] has no direction and is rejected.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: One world-axis component of the direction vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z. Only the ratios between components matter.

Object spelling: give exactly one of axis (a token), vector, or azimuth and elevation, optionally with up as the reference axis for the angles. Choose it when a direction is easier to state as compass angles, e.g. {"azimuth": 30, "elevation": 20} for the direction 30 degrees anticlockwise from +x (seen from above) and 20 degrees above the horizontal plane. The resolved unit vector gives the direction that should appear upwards in the image; Schemaxis removes its component along the viewing direction.
pitfalls: Combining axis, vector and angles in one object fails with OVER_SPECIFIED_DIRECTION.
An omitted azimuth or elevation is taken as 0.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis
Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up
Direction as a world-axis vector [x, y, z] inside the object form; normalised, so only its direction matters. Do not combine it with axis, azimuth or elevation.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.label: Vector

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: One world-axis component of the object's vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

Reference axis for azimuth and elevation in this object: azimuth turns anticlockwise about it (seen from its positive side) starting from +x, or from +y when the reference is along x, and elevation tilts towards it. It is not the camera's screen-up setting.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.label: Angle reference axis

/properties/cameras/items/properties/up/.explanation: Reference axis as a token such as "z+" or "y+"; choose it when angles should be measured about a world axis.
Reference axis as a vector [x, y, z], normalised; choose it when angles should be measured about a tilted axis, such as a vehicle's own vertical.
One world-axis component of the reference axis vector: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: World point [x, y, z] the camera aims at; it is the centre of the image. When set, Schemaxis skips its automatic check that the whole bounds fit inside the frame.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.label: Focal point
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.defaultMeaning: Centre of the framing bounds (the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene, or bounds when given).
pitfalls: Moving the focal point off the bounds centre with automatic scale can crop the model; increase padding or set scale.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.explanation: One world coordinate of the focal point: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/foc.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.explanation: true gives an orthographic projection (no perspective shrinking, sizes comparable across the image) sized by scale; false gives a perspective camera with the lens of a new Blender camera, which Schemaxis does not change (50 mm focal length on a 36 mm sensor).
/properties/cameras/items/properties/par.label: Orthographic
pitfalls: With false, padding and scale have no effect and Schemaxis does not check that the model fits; adjust distance to frame it.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.explanation: Width of the orthographic view in world units: Blender ortho_scale with horizontal sensor fit, so the image spans scale horizontally and scale x height/width vertically. Larger values zoom out. Only used when parallel is true.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.label: Orthographic width
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/sca.defaultMeaning: Automatic: bounds diagonal x (1 + padding) x max(1, width/height), so the shorter image side spans the padded diagonal.
pitfalls: ParaView interprets camera scale as half the view height; the same number frames differently in Blender, and scale values returned by fitCamera or orbitCameras are too small for Blender.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.explanation: Distance from the focal point to the camera along direction. For perspective views it sets how large the model appears; for orthographic views it only moves the camera, but it also sets the far clipping distance (at least distance + 2 x bounds diagonal) while the near clip is 1/10000 of the diagonal.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.label: Camera distance
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/dis.defaultMeaning: Automatic: twice the diagonal of the framing bounds.
pitfalls: In perspective mode, too small a distance places the camera inside the model.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: Framing box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] in world coordinates that replaces the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene for this camera: its centre is the default focal point and its diagonal sets the default scale, distance and clipping. Use it to frame a region of interest or keep framing fixed across states.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.label: Framing bounds
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.defaultMeaning: Union of the bounds of the visible meshes recorded in the saved scene.
pitfalls: The order is min/max per axis, not min corner then max corner; any min greater than its max fails with INVALID_BOUNDS.

/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.explanation: One bound value; positions 0 to 5 are xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/bou.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.explanation: Fractional margin for automatic orthographic framing: the shorter image side spans (1 + padding) times the bounds diagonal, so 0.1 leaves roughly 10% of extra room. Ignored when scale is set or parallel is false.
/properties/cameras/items/properties/pad.label: Padding

/properties/render.explanation: Cycles render settings, world lighting and the single area light applied when the saved scene is rendered. They replace whatever the saved scene contained: omitted keys take the Schemaxis defaults below, not the values saved in the .blend.

/properties/render/properties/device.explanation: Cycles compute backend. CPU renders anywhere and is the reproducible baseline. CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs) or OPTIX (NVIDIA RTX ray-tracing hardware) are faster for many samples; Schemaxis enables only devices of that type, reserves one GPU in workflow scheduling and fails verification unless the device use is evidenced.
/properties/render/properties/device.label: Render device
pitfalls: A GPU backend that the machine or driver lacks fails with DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
GPU and CPU renders of the same scene are not guaranteed to be pixel-identical.

/properties/render/properties/samples.explanation: Cycles samples per pixel (scene.cycles.samples). More samples reduce noise roughly with the square root of the count but cost proportional time; the default is a quick preview. Transmission, emission and small lights need more.
/properties/render/properties/samples.label: Samples

/properties/render/properties/threads.explanation: Fixed number of CPU threads for rendering (render threads mode FIXED). In workflows the operation's execution threads must equal this value, so the scheduler reserves exactly what Blender uses.
/properties/render/properties/threads.label: Render threads
pitfalls: A workflow execution.threads that differs fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; set both together.

/properties/render/properties/denoise.explanation: When true Cycles denoises the final image (use_denoising), giving clean images from few samples at the cost of slightly smoothed fine texture; when false the raw sampled noise remains.
/properties/render/properties/denoise.label: Denoise

/properties/render/properties/transparen.explanation: When true the world background is rendered transparent (film_transparent) for compositing over another background; the world colour still lights the model. When false the background shows worldColour.
/properties/render/properties/transparen.label: Transparent background

/properties/render/properties/seed.explanation: Cycles sampling seed. The same seed and settings reproduce the same noise pattern; changing it gives a different but statistically equivalent noise, useful to check whether a feature is noise.
/properties/render/properties/seed.label: Seed

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: Colour [red, green, blue] of the uniform world background (Background shader), 0 to 1. It is both the visible background and an ambient light from all directions, so it tints the model as well.
/properties/render/properties/worldColou.label: World colour

/properties/render/properties/worldColou.explanation: One channel of the world colour: index 0 red, 1 green, 2 blue, from 0 to 1.

/properties/render/properties/worldStren.explanation: Strength of the world background light. Higher values brighten the background and fill shadows evenly; 0 leaves only the area light (and emission), giving a black background and high contrast.
/properties/render/properties/worldStren.label: World strength

/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.explanation: Radiant power of the single square area light that Schemaxis adds (Blender light energy). The illumination reaching the model falls with the square of the distance from lightPosition, so rescale energy when the model or the light is moved much nearer or farther.
/properties/render/properties/lightEnerg.label: Light power
pitfalls: Small parts lit from a nearby lightPosition need far less energy (the freecad-to-blender example uses 20 W at about 0.4 units).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: World position [x, y, z] of the area light. The light is always aimed at the world origin, not at the model, so for models far from the origin move it accordingly (or move the model to the origin).
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.label: Light position
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [4, -4, 6] (front-right, above, about 8.2 units from the origin).

/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.explanation: One world coordinate of the light position: index 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
/properties/render/properties/lightPosit.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/render/properties/lightSize.explanation: Edge length of the square area light. Larger lights give softer shadow edges; smaller ones give crisper shadows and highlights.
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.label: Light size
/properties/render/properties/lightSize.units: Blender units (scene world units; Schemaxis applies no unit conversion)

/properties/size.explanation: Output image size [width, height] in pixels, each 32 to 2048. The aspect ratio also affects the automatic orthographic width (it widens with width/height). The saved scene's own resolution is ignored.
/properties/size.label: Image size

/properties/size/items.explanation: One image dimension in pixels: index 0 is the width, index 1 the height (32 to 2048).
